# Recipe — add a widget

**Use when:** a screen needs a persistent piece of UI that owns state, subscriptions, or an
affordance of its own — a TopBar, a HUD counter, a quest chip, a currency pill. **Also when it is a
score/HUD readout authored inside a gameplay prefab:** it anchors to a screen edge, so it is a
widget on the `Ui` layer even though everything around it draws through a `Renderer`. That decision
is taken **per object** (rule #16), never once for the whole feature — a board under `WorldRoot` and
a score under `GetHost(RenderLayers.Ui)` is the normal shape, not an inconsistency.

> **In that case Mode A is not available to you.** A uGUI widget cannot be a nested prefab instance
> inside a world-space parent — the parent has no `Canvas` ancestor, so the widget would not render
> at all, and pulling it out of the gameplay prefab is the whole point of the per-object decision.
> Take **Mode B**: the manifest path is forced. Section 1 below still explains both modes, but the
> choice is already made.

**Not** for something anchored to a position in the game's own space that draws through a
`Renderer` — that is a world object ([`add-world-object.md`](./add-world-object.md)). **Not** for a
modal that returns a typed result (that is a dialog —
[`add-dialog.md`](./add-dialog.md)), and **not** for a piece of pure visual behaviour with no state
of its own (that is just a View in `Assets/<Sku>/Views/` — `architecture-map.md` §10).

## 0. The pattern — a pattern, never a service

FR-074. The framework ships `WidgetViewBase`, the `PF/WidgetTemplate` prefab, and this recipe. It
deliberately ships **no `IWidgetService` and no `WidgetBase`**.

A widget controller is a **plain class implementing `IDisposable`**, ctor-injected like everything
else, screen-owned (`Lifetime.Scoped` in the screen's `SceneLifetimeScope`). Do **not** add an
interface or a controller base "for symmetry with `DialogBase`" — a widget's creation leg is trivial
until a second widget proves real duplication. Adding one is a spine change; route it (§6).

Its View is a `WidgetViewBase` subclass and obeys both View tests without exception
(`AGENTS.framework.md` §3): data **in** via `Set*` methods, input **out** via events, no game-state
branching, every method callable in a scene preview with no service resolved.

**Direction of wiring, stated once because it is the most common inversion:** the **controller finds
the View**; a View never resolves, references, or knows its controller. A View that reaches for its
controller cannot pass the gallery test and cannot compile against `Game.Views`' reference set.

---

## 1. Decide the composition mode FIRST

This decision comes **before** the manifest, because it decides whether there is a manifest entry at
all. Two modes, and the choice is not a style preference — it changes what the controller owns, what
the Editor can show, and how many failure modes you inherit.

### Mode A — **authored**: the View is a nested prefab instance in its parent

The widget's View is placed inside the parent prefab at author time. The controller receives the
already-existing View and only wires behaviour to it.

### Mode B — **composed**: the controller instantiates its own prefab at runtime

The widget owns a separate addressable prefab, loads it through `IAssetService`, and instantiates it
under a host `Transform` — either `GetHost(RenderLayers.Ui)` (a screen-level floating widget) or a
slot exposed by a parent View (a sub-widget).

### The decision

**Default to A.** Choose B only when at least one of these is true:

| Choose **B — composed** when | Why A cannot do it |
|---|---|
| **Presence is conditional** — feature flag, A/B arm, tier gate, "only while a quest is active" | An authored instance is always in the prefab |
| **The asset must load separately** — heavy, seasonal, swappable skin, kept out of the parent's bundle | An authored instance ships inside the parent prefab |
| **N copies driven by data** | Author-time authoring cannot express a runtime count — and this case is a **pool**, see §5 |
| **The widget outlives / is shared across screens** (Root-owned persistent widget) | It has no single parent prefab to live in |

Everything else is A.

### What each mode costs

| | **A — authored** | **B — composed** |
|---|---|---|
| Parent prefab shows the real layout in the Editor | ✅ | ❌ — an empty slot; layout is blind until play mode |
| Controller creation leg | `Attach(view)` — synchronous | `CreateAsync(host, ct)` — async, awaited by the owner |
| Owns a `GameObject` | ❌ the parent's prefab owns it | ✅ `Instantiate` → must `Destroy` |
| Owns an Addressables hold | ❌ | ✅ one `Release` per `LoadAsync` (rule #11) |
| Needs its own `Stamp` | ❌ — the parent's recursive `Stamp` already covered it | ✅ — it did not exist when the parent stamped |
| Hides when the owner hides | ✅ automatic (it is in the owner's subtree) | ✅ if mounted in a parent slot · ❌ if mounted under the render-layer host |
| Entry in `game.widgets.json` | ❌ not a scaffold widget — just a View | ✅ scaffolded triple |
| Disposal | unsubscribe only | unsubscribe + `Destroy` + `Release` |

> **The Editor-visibility cost of B is real and is the usual reason a layout ships wrong.** If the
> only thing pushing you to B is "the scaffold makes prefabs", that is not a reason — pick A.

---

## 2A. Mode A — authored

No manifest entry, no `Scaffold.Sync`. The View is a plain `WidgetViewBase` subclass in
`Assets/<Sku>/Views/`, and the nested prefab instance is authored through **Unity-MCP** (rule #12).

**The parent View exposes it** — a purely structural accessor, which passes both View tests because
it branches on nothing and is readable in Prefab Mode:

```csharp
// TopBarView.cs  (Game.Views)
[Tooltip("The quest chip, a nested prefab instance authored inside this prefab.")]
[SerializeField] private TopBarQuestView _quest;

public TopBarQuestView Quest => _quest;
```

**The controller attaches** — no load, no `Instantiate`, no `Destroy`, no `Release`:

```csharp
// TopBarQuestWidget.cs  (Game.Presentation)
public sealed class TopBarQuestWidget : IDisposable
{
    private readonly ISubscriber<QuestProgressed> _progressed;
    private TopBarQuestView _view;
    private IDisposable _sub;
    private bool _disposed;

    public TopBarQuestWidget(ISubscriber<QuestProgressed> progressed) => _progressed = progressed;

    /// <param name="view">Owned by the parent's prefab — this widget does NOT own the GameObject.</param>
    public void Attach(TopBarQuestView view)
    {
        if (view == null) return;              // half-rigged prefab: inert, never throwing
        _view = view;
        _view.ClaimRequested += OnClaimRequested;
        _sub = _progressed.Subscribe(OnQuestProgressed);
    }

    public void Dispose()
    {
        if (_disposed) return;
        _disposed = true;
        if (_sub != null) { _sub.Dispose(); _sub = null; }
        if (_view != null) { _view.ClaimRequested -= OnClaimRequested; _view = null; }
        // No Destroy: the GameObject belongs to the parent's prefab.
    }
}
```

The owner calls `_quest.Attach(_view.Quest);` once its own View exists.

## 2B. Mode B — composed

**Manifest** — `Tools/Codegen/Manifests/Scaffold/game.widgets.json`, append one entry (rule #13 —
never hand-create the prefab, never copy an existing widget folder):

```json
{ "id": "TopBar" }
```

**Run** `Framework/Scaffold/Sync` (editor menu). What lands: `…/Prefabs/TopBarWidget.prefab` (a
**Prefab Variant** of `PF/WidgetTemplate`), `Features/TopBarWidget/Presentation/TopBarWidget.cs`,
`Views/…/TopBarView.cs`. The prefab under `Prefabs/` is scanned into `AssetKeys.TopBarWidget`.

**The controller owns the whole lifetime**, and the failure path must give back exactly what the
success path took:

```csharp
public async UniTask CreateAsync(Transform host, CancellationToken ct)
{
    _prefab = await _assets.LoadAsync(AssetKeys.TopBarWidget, ct);

    // Disposed during the await (screen torn down mid-transition): Dispose already ran and will not
    // run again, so give the hold back here or it leaks for the process lifetime.
    if (_disposed) { ReleasePrefab(); return; }

    try
    {
        _viewGo = UnityEngine.Object.Instantiate(_prefab, host, false);

        // Mandatory. Stamp sets layer + SortingLayer recursively; a parent's earlier Stamp cannot
        // have covered a GameObject that did not exist yet. Band per FR-062
        // (canvas 0 · UI 1–99 · inter-UI FX 100–199 · layer-cover FX 200+).
        _layers.Stamp(_viewGo, RenderLayers.Ui, sortingOrder: 10);

        _view = _viewGo.GetComponent<TopBarView>();
        if (_view == null) throw new InvalidOperationException("…prefab root carries no TopBarView.");

        _view.ShopRequested += OnShopRequested;
        _sub = _walletChanged.Subscribe(OnWalletChanged);   // subscribe BEFORE the first read
        _view.SetCoins(_wallet.Balance(ResourceKeys.Coin));
        _view.SetVisible(false);                            // the owner decides the reveal
    }
    catch { Dispose(); throw; }
}
```

`Dispose()` is **idempotent** (`if (_disposed) return;`) and reverses creation order: unsubscribe →
unhook View events → `Destroy(_viewGo)` → `Release(_prefab)`. The same method serves normal teardown
and the failed-create unwind, so the two paths cannot drift.

> **Mode-B visibility gotcha.** A widget mounted under `GetHost(RenderLayers.Ui)` is a **sibling** of
> the screen's own View, not a child. The screen's `_viewGo.SetActive(false)` in `OnPause`/`OnExit`
> will **not** hide it, and it bleeds through the screen that replaced it. Either mount it in a
> parent slot, or plumb `SetVisible(bool)` through all four of `OnEnter`/`OnPause`/`OnResume`/
> `OnExit`. Mode A never has this problem.

---

## 3. Registration and nesting

Register in the screen's `SceneLifetimeScope`, beside the entry screen:

```csharp
protected override void Configure(IContainerBuilder builder)
{
    builder.RegisterEntryScreen<MainScreen>();
    builder.Register<TopBarWidget>(Lifetime.Scoped).AsSelf();
    builder.Register<TopBarQuestWidget>(Lifetime.Scoped).AsSelf();   // a sub-widget of TopBar
}
```

**The list stays flat no matter how deep the widget tree goes.** Parent/child lives in the
constructors, not in the scope: `MainScreen` takes `TopBarWidget`, `TopBarWidget` takes
`TopBarQuestWidget`, and `MainScreen` never learns that `TopBarQuestWidget` exists. Adding a level
touches exactly two files — the new parent's ctor and this list. Nothing is threaded through
intermediate constructors; that is the difference between DI and hand-rolled `new`.

**Disposal.** A parent disposes its children explicitly, first, in reverse creation order — before
its own `Destroy` removes the subtree under them. Do not rely on container disposal order to
express a parent/child relationship. Double disposal is harmless because `Dispose` is idempotent.

> **Never register a widget `Lifetime.Transient`.** VContainer tracks `IDisposable` instances only
> for `Scoped` and `Singleton`; a `Transient` is **never disposed by the container**. If the owner
> then forgets its explicit `Dispose`, the widget's subscriptions and Addressables hold survive the
> screen. `Scoped` gives you both the explicit parent dispose and the container's backstop at
> `Scope.Teardown()`.

---

## 4. Root-owned persistent widgets — the earned exception

A widget that must survive scene changes is registered in a **Root** installer instead. It then
injects **Root services only**, and screens control **visibility only** — never its lifetime. Same
rule as persistent dialogs. If a screen needs to create, destroy, or reconfigure it, it is not a
persistent widget and belongs to that screen's scope.

## 5. N copies driven by data → pool, not N controllers

A repeated row (quest list, inventory grid, leaderboard entry) is **not** a widget per item. Take a
pool and a View; there is no per-row controller:

```csharp
_rowPool = await _pools.ForPrefabAsync<QuestRowView>(AssetKeys.QuestRow, ct);

var row = _rowPool.Rent();
row.transform.SetParent(_view.QuestSlot, false);
_layers.Stamp(row.gameObject, RenderLayers.Ui, sortingOrder: 11);
…
_rowPool.Return(row);       // Return, never Destroy — the pool owns the instance
```

`IPool<T>` is `Rent` / `Return` / `CountInactive` / `CountRented`. A missing `Return` surfaces as a
`[PoolLeak]` WARN, which is **a bug to fix, not noise** (rule #11, CI grep).

The dividing line: **one instance with its own name and state** → a widget class; **n interchangeable
instances whose count comes from data** → a pool plus a View.

---

## 6. Gate

```
Framework/Scaffold/Check      # mode B only — the prefab-variant + class legs
```

Plus both View tests at review (`AGENTS.framework.md` §3). Mode A adds no scaffold leg, so
`Scaffold/Check` has nothing to say about it — review is the whole gate.

**Visual finish (rule #17).** A widget is something a player looks at, so it ships finished, not
greyboxed: walk the eight-point checklist in the `pf-visual-design` skill and take a capture at FHD in
the SKU's own orientation (1080x1920 portrait, 1920x1080 landscape — never the tool's default). Colours
and spacing come from the SKU's `DesignTokens`, never hardcoded here.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause |
|---|---|
| The layout is wrong and nobody noticed until play mode | Mode B was chosen for an always-present widget. The parent prefab shows an empty slot, so the layout was never reviewable. Move it to mode A. |
| The widget stays on screen over the next screen | Mode B mounted under `GetHost(RenderLayers.Ui)` — a sibling, so the screen's `SetActive(false)` misses it. See the §2B gotcha. |
| The widget is parented correctly but invisible | `Stamp` was skipped, so the subtree is on the wrong Unity layer / SortingLayer and the layer camera does not draw it. A parent's earlier `Stamp` does not cover a later `Instantiate`. |
| Balances/labels leak across a scene change, or a `[PoolLeak]` WARN appears | `Dispose` was never called (registered `Transient`), or the parent destroyed its view without disposing children first. |
| The Addressables hold leaks with no visible symptom | The `if (_disposed) { ReleasePrefab(); return; }` guard after the `await` in `CreateAsync` is missing. |
| Review rejects the View | It branches on game state, or it holds a reference to its controller. The controller finds the View; never the reverse. |
| A `.prefab` diff is enormous and full of fileID churn | The nested instance was authored by editing YAML. Revert and redo through Unity-MCP (rule #12). |
